pr_body:
For the motivation please check  #74659, but in very short: initializer functions (with `__attribute__((__constructor__))` are not exclusive to C++, but are also used by some libraries. Zephyr not supporting them without C++ means those libraries will not work as intended. This PR fixes this by allowing running those initializers also without enabling C++.

* Move ctors and init_array initialization from the CPP library to the kernel library, as this is common for both C and C++ and it is the kernel who is running it.
* Rename z_cpp_init_static to z_init_static, and have the kernel always call it.
* Rename the hidden kconfig option `CONFIG_CPP_STATIC_INIT_GNU` to `CONFIG_STATIC_INIT_GNU` instead. Have this option default to y only if building with CPP, or for native/posix arch targets, or if COVERAGE is enabled (see below why).
* If `STATIC_INIT_GNU` is not selected verify there is no constructors left behind and generate a build error otherwise.
* Rename common-rom-cpp.ld to common-rom-init.ld

Fixes #74659
Fixes #74601

------

The choice of default to y only in some cases, is motivated by not wanting to increase the image size unnecessarily.
The current defaults y being by CPP (which requires it for constructors, and had it before), NATIVE_BUILD (for ex. native_sim) where we don't mind 100bytes of extra code size and prefer to ensure we don't leave constructors forgotten by default, and COVERAGE, which in some implementations ( https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Freestanding-Environments.html ) also uses initializer functions.

Thanks @andyross. So far I was moving it to lib/libc but I can put it anywhere you think is best. Just say where :)

I think it can move to kernel/ -- that's where the constructors are called from now. The problem is that this will add a small amount of code to every build, even those which don't use constructors. Supporting both ctors and init_array segments will probably take dozens of LOC. In an ideal world, we'd discover if there are any of these present in the rest of the system before building the code which handles them.

Change the Kconfig variable `CPP_STATIC_INIT_GNU` to `STATIC_INIT_GNU` so that we continue to leave these out of the arc MWDT builds.

issue_context.title: Zephyr does not run functions with __attribute__((__constructor__)) on init unless CONFIG_CPP=y
issue_context.body:
This is a set of 2 very related bugs

## 1st. Zephyr does not run functions with `__attribute__((__constructor__))` on init unless CONFIG_CPP=y

**Describe the bug**
Unless CONFIG_CPP is set, Zephyr does not execute during init functions with `__attribute__((__constructor__)) `
(i.e. functions in .ctors or .init_array sections) or manually placed in this sections.
This is not correct behavior, as this is not CPP exclusive, and some libraries rely on this behavior. For example
https://github.com/picolibc/picolibc/blob/main/newlib/libc/ssp/stack_protector.c#L20 

On the other hand if CONFIG_CPP is set, this will be correctly called together with C++ object constructors.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
Modify hello world like so:
```diff
diff --git a/samples/hello_world/src/main.c b/samples/hello_world/src/main.c
index c550ab461cb..c4994a4aba9 100644
--- a/samples/hello_world/src/main.c
+++ b/samples/hello_world/src/main.c
@@ -5,6 +5,13 @@
  */
 
 #include <stdio.h>
+#include <string.h>
+
+__attribute__((__constructor__))
+void foobar(void)
+{
+       printf("hello from embedded function with attribute constructor\n");
+}
 
 int main(void)
 {
```
1. mkdir build; cd build
2. cmake -GNinja -DBOARD=qemu_x86 ../samples/hello_world/
3. ninja run
4. See there is no "hello from embedded function with attribute constructor" printed.
```
SeaBIOS (version zephyr-v1.0.0-0-g31d4e0e-dirty-20200714_234759-fv-az50-zephyr)
Booting from ROM..
*** Booting Zephyr OS build v3.7.0-rc1-196-g5e295ac39ebd ***
Hello World! qemu_x86/atom
```

1. mkdir build; cd build
2. cmake -GNinja -DBOARD=qemu_x86 ../samples/hello_world/ -DCONFIG_CPP=y
3. ninja run
4. See "hello from embedded function with attribute constructor" is printed.
```
SeaBIOS (version zephyr-v1.0.0-0-g31d4e0e-dirty-20200714_234759-fv-az50-zephyr)
Booting from ROM..
*** Booting Zephyr OS build v3.7.0-rc1-196-g5e295ac39ebd ***
hello from embedded function with attribute constructor  <--------------
Hello World! qemu_x86/atom
```

**Expected behavior**
Functions w `__attribute__((__constructor__)) ` (in  .ctors or .init_array sections) called even if CONFIG_CPP is not set

## 2nd. Functions w `__attribute__((__constructor__))` in native_sim are run before Zephyr is booted unless CONFIG_CPP=y

Due to the issues described above, as those .ctors and .init_array sections are forgotten by Zephyr's linker script unless CONFIG_CPP=y, the final link of the native_simulator runner will pick them. On runtime the host libC, while initializing the native_simulator runner, will call into them.
This will call this embedded functions to be executed in the context of the runner, before anything related to Zephyr is initialized , which is likely to cause trouble.
If on the other hand CONFIG_CPP=y is set for the Zephyr image, they will be properly called during Zephyr boot and only then.

**To Reproduce**
For extra context, we modify the sample a bit more:
```diff
diff --git a/samples/hello_world/src/runnery.c b/samples/hello_world/src/runnery.c
new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..4b2e13ac551
--- /dev/null
+++ b/samples/hello_world/src/runnery.c
@@ -0,0 +1,7 @@
+#include <stdio.h>
+
+__attribute__((__constructor__))
+void foobar_runner (void)
+{
+       printf("hello from host/runner context function with attribute constructor\n");
+}
diff --git a/samples/hello_world/CMakeLists.txt b/samples/hello_world/CMakeLists.txt
index ecb7d24bb8f..6c26da39b6b 100644
--- a/samples/hello_world/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/samples/hello_world/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -6,3 +6,5 @@ find_package(Zephyr REQUIRED HINTS $ENV{ZEPHYR_BASE})
 project(hello_world)
 
 target_sources(app PRIVATE src/main.c)
+
+target_sources(native_simulator INTERFACE src/runnery.c)
```

1.cmake -GNinja -DBOARD=native_sim ../samples/hello_world/ 
2.ninja && ./zephyr/zephyr.exe
```
hello from embedded function with attribute constructor
hello from host/runner context function with attribute constructor
*** Booting Zephyr OS build v3.7.0-rc1-196-g5e295ac39ebd ***
Hello World! native_sim/native
```
3. See that "hello from embedded function with attribute constructor" appears before Zephyr's boot and next to hello from host/runner context function with attribute constructor

On the other hand
1.cmake -GNinja -DBOARD=native_sim ../samples/hello_world/  -DCONFIG_CPP=y
2.ninja && ./zephyr/zephyr.exe
```
hello from host/runner context function with attribute constructor
*** Booting Zephyr OS build v3.7.0-rc1-197-g66ef30d8c633 ***
hello from embedded function with attribute constructor
Hello World! native_sim/native
```
3. Properly runs the embedded constructor at Zephyr boot.

**Expected behavior**
Functions w `__attribute__((__constructor__)) ` (in  .ctors or .init_array sections) called from the Zephyr embedded context even if CONFIG_CPP=y is not set and not from the runner context.

-------

**Impact**
Some applications/libraries will not initialize properly

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux, Ubuntu 22.04
 - Toolchain (e.g Zephyr SDK, ...): 0.16.8
 - Commit SHA or Version used: main as of now: 5e295ac39ebd7a732cc064cdf72433f16392b021

**Additional context**
Related to #74601 (which is a particular bug due to this behaviour)
Related to #39347 , #36907, #46357, 8e35cc8eb4ec10f50819fa402dbc3c44b6bd25ca which added or improved the handling of these sections
comments:
Given that I seem to be the first one to realize (or at least report this), and that the only bug I'm aware related to this has a workaround queued, I will set it as low priority.
But this would make picolibc's stack-protector not work as expected on embedded targets. Apart from being the underlying cause for the issue described here #74601

FWIW, the code to call those is in lib/cpp/abi and predicated on CONFIG_CPP_STATIC_INIT_GNU=y.  My guess is if @keith-packard saw it happen it was because there's some code in the libc that's duplicating it.

It shouldn't be hard to unwrap that and make it universal; maybe just move it into somewhere near the top of z_cstart() in kernel/init.c...

> This used to work.

@keith-packard what I can see is that for embedded targets (tried for qemu_x86), the stack-protector code is called properly except for the init function, and still detects and reports the failures.

Yeah, when I dug in I noticed that only Zephyr constructors using SYS_INIT were run from C applications. We've got two nearly identical solutions in #74682 and #74700; both of those will increase ROM usage for all Zephyr C applications.

review_comments: Let's pull this code into init.c so it can be in-lined into bg_thread_main instead of being a separate function. It's tiny, and merging should make the resulting code smaller.

As commented here https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/74682#issuecomment-2185273088 , I think it is best to just leave it as is by now. This PR only moves code which already exists and enables it without CPP without optimizing it further.
